title: Eosinophil–neutrophil spline coupling fails temporal lung-function transfer: a rare-tail stress test in NHANES
abstract: A fixed eosinophil-neutrophil spline interaction failed to improve temporal FEV1/FVC prediction beyond additive cell counts and standard covariates in NHANES 2007-08 to 2009-10 (n=3,996): weighted MSE gain -312.741 percentage-points squared. Rare outside-training-range observations dominated the failure; post-hoc physically bounded predictions gave gain -0.219 (conditional 95% PSU-bootstrap interval -0.525 to 0.113), not evidence that physiological coupling is absent. Source PSU-grouped cross-validation also favored the additive baseline. Separate cross-sectional surveys provide within-platform temporal validation, not external-institution or longitudinal validation. All checks were performed by the AI author.
